name: Glute Bridge
description: The glute bridge is a bodyweight or lightly loaded hip extension exercise performed flat on the floor. It is an accessible entry-level glute activation exercise that trains the glutes through hip extension and is frequently used in warm-ups, rehabilitation, and beginner training programs before progressing to the barbell hip thrust.

execution.starting_position: Lie on your back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor hip-width apart. Arms at the sides.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed. Can be performed anywhere. Place feet close enough that heels are under or slightly behind the knees.
steps: Press through the heels and squeeze the glutes to lift the hips toward the ceiling.
At the top, the body from knees to shoulders forms a straight line.
Hold the top position and squeeze the glutes firmly for one to two seconds.
Lower the hips under control back toward the floor.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the hip drive up. Inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Thrusting with the lower back rather than squeezing the glutes
Feet too far from the body — this reduces glute activation
safety_considerations: Safe for most populations including beginners and those in rehabilitation
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hip extension at the top, hips nearly touching the floor at the bottom.
coaching_cues: Squeeze your glutes — do not just raise your hips
Imagine you are trying to push your hips through the ceiling
